- If sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to underreact — increase forecast slightly above recent mean.
- If sentiment is strongly bearish (≤ -0.33) and price is trending down, model often overcorrects — reduce forecast by 1–2% to avoid premature bottoming.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots — cap forecast at +3–5% above peak for next 5–7 days.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (±0.33), model often fails to capture mean reversion — adjust forecast to align with 10–15-day moving average of history.
- If model shows flat 30-day trend but true outcome shows strong divergence (e.g., >5% from mean), sentiment history should trigger a 1–2% upward adjustment if bullish, or downward if bearish.
- For 30-day forecasts, if last 3–5 days show strong sentiment reversal (e.g., from +0.67 to -0.33), model often lags — add 1–2% buffer to forecast to account for lagged sentiment effect.
